stem: Seven of ten offspring show a target trait, and a grower concludes the trait follows an exact 3:1 inheritance ratio. What is the main problem with that conclusion?
choices: A sample of ten is too small to establish an exact segregation model; larger and replicated populations are needed.
A 7:3 result is close enough to 3:1 that replication matters mainly for estimating how strongly the environment affects expression of the trait.
The observed proportion can support a simple inheritance model, but the generation label must be confirmed before sample size becomes important.
A small family can reveal the correct ratio when the trait is visually clear, so the main limitation is whether all offspring were scored at the same age.
rationale: Small populations are strongly affected by sampling variation. Observed proportions should not be treated as proof of a genetic model without adequate population size and replication.
